summary: Backend-only regression + targeted coverage for iter14 refactors: approve_quote(), upload_completion_photo(), and description-aware AI image cache. Authored /app/backend/tests/test_quote_approval_completion_refactor.py with 12 tests across three suites: TestApproveQuoteEndpoint (5 — approve no-price-change, reject, 404, 400-not-pending, higher-price → booking flips to pending_customer_approval with token + original/adjusted price), TestCompletionPhotoUpload (4 — 404 missing booking, 400 wrong status, 400 non-image, success persists photo + note under /app/backend/static/completion_photos), TestDescriptionAwareImageCache (3 — same image+desc HITS, same image with different desc MISSES (creates a 2nd image_cache row keyed on cache_key), and refactor introduced cache_key field + index). Combined regression run against public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL: 69/69 PASSED (50 prior + 7 iter13 + 12 new). Refactor preserves all observable behavior. ONE pre-existing backend bug surfaced while writing tests: `completion_note: str = ""` on the upload_completion_photo signature lacks `Form()` annotation, so FastAPI treats it as a QUERY parameter, not multipart form data. Frontends sending it as form data silently drop the note. Test was adjusted to pass it via params= to validate the success path.

minor.issue: `completion_note: str = ""` parameter is missing the `Form()` annotation, so FastAPI binds it as a QUERY parameter instead of multipart form data. Any client sending it in the multipart body (the obvious choice given file is also multipart) silently drops the note — request still returns 200 but completion_note is stored as ''. PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by iter14 refactor); refactor only moved the same buggy signature into _persist_completion_metadata. Fix: change to `completion_note: str = Form(default="")`.

_process_quote_price_increase silently swallows ALL exceptions from send_sms (Twilio outage, bad phone format, etc.) while still flipping the booking to pending_customer_approval. The customer is now waiting for an SMS that will never arrive, with no log alarm beyond a warning line. Consider either (a) propagating a 502 with a 'try again' hint, or (b) queuing a retry job.

When approved_price <= original_price, _process_quote_price_increase is skipped — but the existing booking is left untouched (no original_price, no token). If the same quote was previously price-increased (and the booking is in pending_customer_approval), then re-approved at the original price, the stale customer_approval_token + adjusted_price fields remain in the booking. Add an explicit 'clear price-adjustment fields' branch on the equal-or-lower path.

action_items: Fix completion_note parameter binding: change to `completion_note: str = Form(default="")` in upload_completion_photo signature so multipart-form clients can actually populate it.

(Optional) On approve_quote with approved_price <= original, explicitly $unset booking.customer_approval_token / adjusted_price / original_price / requires_customer_approval to avoid stale state on re-approval.
(Optional) Surface SMS failures in _process_quote_price_increase to the caller rather than warn-logging — the customer is otherwise stranded in pending_customer_approval forever.
critical_code_review_comments: approve_quote refactor is clean and idiomatic; helpers are correctly scoped. Minor: _build_quote_update sets approval_status='approved' even when the booking-price branch will then overwrite it to 'approved_pending_customer'. The first write is wasted but harmless — consider either computing the final status up-front or moving update_data['approval_status'] = 'approved_pending_customer' onto a return value of _process_quote_price_increase to keep the data flow explicit.

_send_quote_approval_decision_email reads `booking = await db.bookings.find_one({"quote_id": quote_id})` independently from _process_quote_price_increase which already did the same lookup. Two DB round-trips per approval; pass the booking down or memoize.

_save_completion_photo uses `datetime.now()` (naive local time) for the filename suffix, while the rest of server.py uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`. Two completions in the same wall-clock second will overwrite each other (rare but real). Use uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] in the filename or include microseconds.

_save_completion_photo + _persist_completion_metadata are NOT transactional. If the DB update fails for any reason (race, connection drop), the file is now left orphaned on disk. The wrapper try/except cleans up only when _persist_completion_metadata raises HTTPException — `update_one` returning `matched_count==0` does raise 404 (good), but a connection error would propagate up the wrapper and trigger photo_path.unlink() (also good). Verified the cleanup branch is correct.

Description-aware cache key uses sha256(image_hash + '|' + desc_norm). desc_norm only does .strip().lower() — no Unicode NFC normalization, no whitespace collapse. 'heavy items' and 'heavy  items' (double space) will MISS and re-bill the AI. Apply re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', desc).strip().lower() for deterministic keying.

_check_image_cache deletes the local compressed file on a HIT but the SAME file is unlinked AGAIN at line ~805 in analyze_image_for_quote on the MISS-then-success path. Currently fine because the cache HIT returns early, but if a future refactor moves the unlink earlier the second call will FileNotFoundError. Centralize compressed-file cleanup in a try/finally.

image_cache documents now retain `description_norm` plus the full `breakdown` payload — these are unbounded in size. Add a TTL index (e.g. 90 days) so the collection doesn't grow forever; the iter14 PR added a `cache_key` index but no TTL.

server.py is now 3878 lines (was 3865 in iter13). Approve_quote helpers (~150 lines) + completion helpers (~80 lines) + the 4 quote_*_html builders (~250 lines) are now obvious extraction candidates into routers/quotes.py and routers/bookings.py + emails/templates.py.

rca of the issue: test_completion_upload_success_persists_path_and_note initially failed because completion_note arrived as '' even though the test sent data={'completion_note': note}. Root cause: in /app/backend/server.py line 1940 the parameter is declared `completion_note: str = ""` without a `Form()` marker. FastAPI's body-parsing logic only treats parameters as form fields when explicitly annotated; otherwise (and with another non-body param like `booking_id` already in the path), it falls back to query-parameter binding. Mitigation in the test: send via `params=` instead of `data=`. Mitigation in production: add `from fastapi import Form` and annotate `completion_note: str = Form(default="")`.
